hero.h1: Trenchless Sewer Repair in Ravenswood, Chicago
hero.sub: On a Ravenswood lot, the sewer line runs under the front garden, the walk and often a parkway tree. Trenchless repair rebuilds the pipe through small openings, so most of that stays where it is. Our office is on Ravenswood Avenue.

blocks.body: Trenchless sewer repair, also called no-dig sewer repair, fixes a damaged pipe without digging a trench along its full length. Instead of opening up your yard from the house to the street, we work through one or two access points and repair the pipe from the inside or replace it in place. There are two main methods: cured-in-place pipe (CIPP) lining and pipe bursting. Both fix the line underground, so what's above it stays untouched.

blocks.h2: Trenchless Repair on a Narrow City Lot
blocks.body: A Ravenswood lot is often 25 or 30 feet wide, with a building close to the sidewalk and a garage on the alley. There isn't much room for a trench, a pile of dirt and an excavator. Trenchless repair needs only a small opening at each end of the damaged section. That keeps the work off the stoop, out of the gangway and away from neighbors' foundations. We plan the openings around what you'd rather not have disturbed.

blocks.h2: Trenchless Sewer Questions From Ravenswood Homeowners

items.q: Can a century-old clay sewer be lined?
items.preview: Often, if it holds its shape.
items.answer: Often. If it's cracked but round, it can be lined.

items.q: Does sewer work need a city permit?
items.answer: Sewer repairs in Chicago usually need a permit. We handle the paperwork for our work.

items.q: How long does a liner last?
items.answer: Liners are designed to last for decades.

items.q: Will the building be without plumbing?
items.answer: Usually only for part of the day.

items.q: Can you work from the alley side?
items.answer: Sometimes, depending on where the line runs. The camera tells us.

items.q: How much does trenchless sewer repair cost in Ravenswood?
items.preview: It depends on length, depth and method. You'll approve a flat price first.
items.answer: It depends on how much of the line needs work, the depth, the method and access. You'll approve a flat-rate price before we start.
